  Flexible administration windows let students test when they are ready, but they break
  the assumption that every score comes from the same point in the school year. We show
  that a diagnostic classification model with window-specific attribute profiles recovers
  growth estimates within 0.04 of a fixed-window baseline.

# Introduction

Assessment systems built for a single spring window inherit a convenient fiction: that
all students in a grade encounter the same content at the same time.

## Why flexible administration changes reporting

The reporting layer, not the scoring layer, absorbs most of the difficulty.

- Window membership is recorded at the student level, not the school level.
- Attribute profiles are estimated jointly across windows with a shared item bank.
- Growth is reported as a change in mastery probability.

### Scope of this report

Sections 2 and 3 develop the model and simulation evidence. The model builds on diagnostic
classification models [@templin2013; @bradshaw2019] and is estimated with measr [@measr].

# Measurement model {blurb="Specification, estimation, and the assumptions that let windows be compared."}

## Estimating growth across windows

Take a look at the image in @fig-penguins.

```{r}
#| label: fig-penguins
#| fig-cap: |
#|   Here is a figure captions.
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Alt text for the image

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = bill_len, y = flipper_len)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = species))
```

::: {.callout-note}
Credible intervals are computed from 4 chains of 2,000 post-warmup draws.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
Growth estimates should not be reported for attributes measured by fewer than five items.
:::

And here is a table, as shown in @tbl-example.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-example
#| tbl-cap: Here is a table caption.

tibble(
  state = sample(state.name, size = 10),
  size = sample(50:100, size = 10)
) |>
  mutate(pct = size / sum(size) * 100) |>
  gt() |>
  gt_theme_report()
```

W. Jake Thompson, PhD, is the Associate Director for Research and Psychometrics at Accessible Teaching, Learning, and Assessment Systems (ATLAS), a research center within the Achievement and Assessment Institute at the University of Kansas.
He received his PhD in Educational Psychology and Research from the University of Kansas's School of Education and Human Sciences in 2018, with a focus on research, evaluation, measurement, and statistics.
